NASDAQ 100 Technical Analysis
Daily price chart of the NASDAQ 100 testing the key 30,000.0 resistance level during early Monday trading. Source: TradingView

The Nasdaq 100 looks pretty positive here early on Monday morning, as we are threatening the 30,000 level almost immediately. With this being the case, it looks like the buyers are back. The fear is starting to subside a bit, and it is probably worth noting that here in the last few minutes, we have seen the 10-year yield roll over pretty significantly.

So, I think one of the headlines out there is that Trump is always open to talking, and Iran has to come to the table. It at least opens up the possibility of peace. That obviously would be a huge bonus for everybody involved.

Dow Jones 30 Technical Analysis
Daily price chart of the Dow Jones 30 recovering to 52,121.00 while approaching moving average resistance. Source: TradingView

The Dow Jones 30 has risen quite nicely as well. It looks a lot like a market that is trying to break free again. The 50-day EMA could cause a little bit of a headache for buyers as potential resistance, but ultimately, this is a market that is in a longer-term uptrend. We have had a nice little pullback here. Maybe we are trying to turn to a new leg higher.

It is a little early to say that, but if we can get some relief in those interest rates, it certainly would not be a bad thought.

S&P 500 Technical Analysis
Daily price chart of the S&P 500 showing price reclaiming 7,709.50 as bulls target the 7,800 level. Source: TradingView

The S&P 500 finds itself rallying as well. This is a market that is now breaking 7,700. That is a big victory, and overall, this does look like a market that is trying to get to the 7,800 level before it is all said and done.

The 7,600 level was support. It did get violated, and we drove all the way down to 7,520 or so. We have had a nice bounce since then. We are back above the 50-day EMA. One would think that is a good sign.

We are in an uptrend. That has not changed, so it looks pretty positive so far here on Monday.

By 05:56 a.m. ET (09:56 GMT), the Dow futures contract had risen 354 points, or 0.7%, S&P 500 futures had climbed 51 points, or 0.7%, and Nasdaq 100 futures had gained 326 points, or 1.1%.

The gains followed a mixed session on Wall Street Friday, when the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite both advanced while the Dow Jones Industrial Average edged lower.

Here are some of the biggest premarket U.S. stock movers today:

Crypto-linked stocks climbed in premarket trading, tracking a sharp rebound in Bitcoin, which reached its highest level in more than seven months.

Bitcoin was up 5.1% at $84,435.90, taking its weekly gain to roughly 5%. The cryptocurrency had briefly fallen below $76,000 following the Federal Reserve's rate decision before recovering over the weekend.

The rebound came after a U.S. regulatory decision expanded the scope for on-chain trading of tokenized stocks, while lower oil prices helped ease broader inflation concerns. Investors also appeared to look beyond the hawkish tone that followed last week's Fed rate increase, which lifted the benchmark rate to 4.00%.

MicroStrategy jumped about 7% premarket, while Coinbase and Robinhood rose 4.8% and 3.7%, respectively.

Bitcoin miners also advanced, with MARA Holdings and Riot Platforms each gaining nearly 5%, Hut 8 rising 4.8% and CleanSpark adding 4.3%.

AI-related stocks also moved higher after a sharp selloff a week earlier triggered by warnings from executives at major artificial intelligence companies about the risks surrounding the technology.

Investors appeared to refocus on evidence that spending on AI development and infrastructure remains strong.

Intel rose 5.4% in premarket trading, while Marvell Technology gained 2.6%, Meta Platforms added 2.4% and Dell Technologies climbed 2.7%.

The moves suggest that investor attention has shifted back toward the potential growth from continued AI investment after concerns over the pace and sustainability of spending weighed on the sector last week.

Warner Bros. Discovery jumped 7.9% in premarket trading, while Paramount Skydance gained 6.8% after a report said Paramount and California's attorney general were in advanced settlement talks that could remove one of the final hurdles to the companies' proposed $110 billion merger.

US stock futures advanced on Monday as investors assessed developments in the Middle East, declining oil prices and artificial intelligence policy discussions between Washington and Beijing.

At 06:58 GMT, Dow Jones Industrial Average futures were up 239 points, or 0.5%, while S&P 500 futures gained 39 points, also rising 0.5%. Nasdaq 100 futures advanced 218 points, or 0.7%.

Wall Street ended Friday's session with mixed results. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite closed higher, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined slightly.

US Treasury yields increased across maturities as market expectations for another Federal Reserve interest rate increase before the end of 2026 remained broadly unchanged.

Analysts at Vital Knowledge attributed much of Friday's equity market gains to companies supplying infrastructure and components for artificial intelligence, including semiconductor manufacturers.

The analysts also noted that the Bank of Japan's latest interest rate increase was less restrictive than some investors had anticipated, with two policymakers voting to leave rates unchanged.

The yen weakened following the decision, prompting concerns among the analysts about the possibility of Japanese authorities selling US Treasury securities to support the currency.

Fighting in Yemen Raises Shipping Concerns

Investors continued to monitor the conflict in Yemen after reports of intensified fighting between Iran-backed Houthi forces and Saudi-aligned groups over the weekend.

The New York Times, citing a Saudi army officer, reported clashes in mountainous areas of southwestern Yemen on Sunday.

The fighting comes amid competition for positions near the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a shipping passage connecting the Gulf of Aden with the Red Sea.

Saudi Arabia has increasingly relied on this route to export crude oil following disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

According to The New York Times, the Houthis also said they had launched missiles and drones towards Riyadh and targeted Saudi oil facilities in response to Saudi air strikes inside Yemen.

The reported attacks and military developments have added uncertainty to the outlook for regional shipping and energy exports.

Brent Crude Falls as Saudi Exports Recover

Oil prices declined on Monday despite continued tensions between the United States and Iran.

US President Donald Trump threatened further action against Iran's leadership if Tehran did not pursue an agreement, while Iranian military officials warned of retaliation against renewed attacks.

U.S. stock futures are trending higher early Monday as investors digest a stark warning from President Donald Trump to Iran alongside cooling crude oil prices, while looking ahead to a week of key consumer retail earnings.

The Polymarket (CRYPTO: POL) crowd is heavily bullish for the Sept. 21 trading session. The "S&P 500 (SPX) Up or Down on September 21?" contract currently reflects an 81% chance of a higher open.

Why That Number Matters

Traders are navigating a mix of geopolitical escalations, AI sector debates, and a busy week of economic insights:

Positive Index Futures: Equity futures point to a green open across major benchmarks. Dow Jones futures rose 0.35%. S&P 500 futures advanced 0.41%. Nasdaq 100 futures gained 0.56%, and Russell 2000 futures ticked up 0.34%.

Geopolitics & Energy: President Trump warned Iran of severe economic consequences or the destruction of its leadership if Tehran refuses to reach a deal. Iran's military responded by threatening sustained retaliation against U.S. bases. The confrontation widened over the weekend with Houthi missile and drone strikes on sensitive targets in Riyadh. Despite this, oil prices retreated; Brent crude dropped to $102.05 a barrel, down 1.75%, and WTI crude fell to $94.33 by 1.82%.

AI Developments: Over the weekend, President Trump polled the public on renaming artificial intelligence, suggesting terms like "Superior Intelligence," and proposed a new "AI Force" and an "AI Czar" to monitor the industry. This comes as the U.S. and China prepare for bilateral discussions covering AI safety, with China recently accusing the U.S. of applying "naked double standards" on AI model distillation.

The Bull Case and Market Outlook

Despite the recent wave of central bank rate hikes, the global stock bull market remains remarkably resilient, according to Ed Yardeni. "Central banks in the US, Europe, and Japan all raised their policy rates over the last two weeks," yet "neither development has broken the global stock bull market, as earnings forecasts keep getting marked up," he said.

Investing.com - SpaceX's weighting in the Nasdaq 100 Index will more than double to 2.82% when the benchmark's quarterly rebalance takes effect on Monday, Bloomberg reported, citing data from the index provider.

Looking for the next multi-bagger? This AI enabler is up 90%+ since picked by our AI models in July -- and still has a 62% upside »

The adjustment, calculated using Friday's closing prices, confirms a provisional weighting that will begin to align the space and satellite giant's influence in the index with its massive market valuation.

SpaceX, which made its public debut in July, currently holds a relatively small 1.28% weighting in the gauge. Most of its shares were locked up following its listing, constraining its index representation even after Nasdaq revised its rules to allow newly listed mega-cap companies to enter the index sooner without requiring a 10% free-float minimum.

The rebalance helps close an unusual disparity: while SpaceX ranks as the seventh-largest company in the Nasdaq 100 with a market capitalization exceeding $2 trillion, its current weighting does not even place it among the top 20 constituents by percentage weight.

Mechanical buying for passive funds

The sharp increase in index weight will force passive funds and exchange-traded funds (ETFs) tracking the benchmark to adjust their portfolios and purchase billions of dollars in SpaceX stock to maintain proper tracking accuracy.

Major funds affected by the rebalance include:

Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 [(QQQ)]: The $482 billion fund is one of the largest ETFs in the world tracking the Nasdaq 100.

Global Benchmark Products: Over 200 investment products track the Nasdaq 100, managing more than $800 billion in total assets globally.

The Nasdaq 100 tracks the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange. While inclusion does not require a minimum market capitalization threshold, companies must maintain an average daily volume of at least 200,000 shares alongside other liquidity requirements.
